newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Sonora state breeder cattle herd still down.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Sonora state breeder cattle herd still down.

text.p: Breeder cattle numbers in Sonora state, one of Mexico's top livestock regions, are down around 40,000 head in the last two years, the state-owned news agency Notimex said Tuesday.
Arnoldo Molina Hernandez, an official from Sonora's livestock development ministry, told Notimex that drought problems still persist and are not helping the re-building of the state herd.
Molina said he believed 1996 numbers dipped below 800,000 head, from the 808,000 registered in 1995 and the 840,000 in 1994. He said specific updated figures had not yet been made available.

Most of northern Mexico suffered serious rain shortages in 1994-1995 and were only partially alleviated in certain areas during 1996, as hurricanes brought the first substantial rains in dozens of months. Some areas are still suffering drought conditions.
